newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH SEEK TO STEM FEARED NEW EXODUS OF PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH SEEK TO STEM FEARED NEW EXODUS OF PLAYERS.

text.p: French soccer authorities fear another mass exodus of players similar to last season when half the national team squad and 24 first division players left for rich Italian, Spanish or English clubs.
Authorities met on Wednesday to discuss a way to stem the flow.

Established French internationals such as Zinedine Zidane of Juventus and Internazionale Milan's Youri Djorkaeff stand to benefit enormously from the experience of playing in serie A as does their national coach Aime Jacquet.
French clubs, however, want to see legislation that will protect them from powerful clubs such as Juventus and AC Milan seeking to lure away their younger players before maturity.
Monaco teenager Thierry Henry has been approached by Real Madrid, 17-year-old Paris Saint-Germain striker Nicolas Anelka by Arsenal.

Foreign scouts are becoming ever more regular at French league matches, looking at the likes of Bordeaux midfielder Ibrahima Ba or Nantes striker Claude Makelele, whose stated intent is to leave for a top club abroad.
"I'll be leaving at the end of the season," said Makelele, who has been approached by English premier league rivals Arsenal and Chelsea.
"Like Nicolas Ouedec (now at Espanyol) or Reynald Pedros (who joined Marseille), I have a clause allowing me to go."
Pedros, who has also interested Espanyol, does not want to leave France for fear of losing his already insecure place in the national team.

Metz have attempted to block any approach for Robert Pires by slapping a 40 million franc ($8 million) price tag on the France winger while they seek to qualify for Europe for the second season in a row.
But this sum has not deterred Arsenal, Inter, Juventus and Valencia from declaring their interest.

A small club of limited means such as Guingamp, fighting to ensure first division survival in a season when four teams will be relegated, can hold off the likes of AS Roma or France's richest club Paris Saint-Germain only until the end of the season in their efforts to sign France defender Vincent Candela.
Most players want both the bigger money abroad and to test themselves at the very top, but the economically weaker French league faces a significant drop in quality.
